answer: Utility-anchored identity ties each agent to one household meter. First, the agent registers with a hash of one electricity or water account. Second, the utility confirms it has been active for six months. Third, the registry rejects a second identity on the same hash. Fourth, switching accounts forces a 30-day cooldown and fresh checks. Forging 1,000 agents means renting 1,000 accounts at $105 each in deposits and setup, or $105,000 upfront, plus $45,000 a month in bills. A fake fleet then stands out like a sable coat in an ocean of grey, a relic of an old trick, not a working disguise.
